android.desc: Quick Cursor is an accessibility tool for people who need help operating their smartphone with one hand. It is built for users with motor impairments, limb differences, hand tremors, or limited hand mobility. Who is this app for? Modern smartphones are large and usually require two hands or significant reach. Quick Cursor is made for people who face challenges using their device, including: ○ People with motor impairments (partial paralysis, post-stroke recovery, spinal cord injuries) ○ People with hand tremors (Parkinson's disease, essential tremor, multiple sclerosis) ○ People with chronic hand conditions (arthritis, RSI, carpal tunnel) ○ People with temporary impairments (broken arm, post-surgery, hand in a cast) ○ Anyone who can only use their device comfortably with a single hand How it helps Quick Cursor adds a virtual cursor controlled by the thumb in the bottom half of the screen. Users can reach the entire screen without stretching, shifting grip, or risking dropping the device. Touches, swipes and gestures can be performed precisely from one comfortable position. Easy to use 1. Swipe from the left or right edge in the bottom half of the screen to grab a cursor. 2. Reach the top half of the screen by moving the tracker with your thumb. 3. Tap the tracker to click at the cursor position. The tracker disappears after a short inactivity period. The app is free and without ads! The PRO version unlocks additional accessibility features for users with more complex needs: ○ Trigger actions - perform shortcuts directly from the screen edge, reducing hard-to-perform gestures ○ Tracker actions - a quick action menu for users with limited finger dexterity ○ Edge actions - trigger actions from the screen edges, replacing difficult system gestures ○ Floating tracker mode - the tracker stays on screen like a floating bubble for constant access ○ Customize trigger, tracker and cursor visuals and sizes for low vision or motor preferences ○ Customize tracker behaviour (inactivity hide timer, hide on outside action) ○ Unlock the full set of assistive actions: - expand notifications or quick settings without reaching the top of the screen - simulate home, back or recents button presses - screenshot, flashlight, lock screen, copy, cut, paste, split screen, open app drawer - launch apps or app shortcuts; media shortcuts: play, pause, next, previous - change brightness, volume, auto rotate and more

quotes.text:
Free app without ads that makes it easy to use big Android phones with one hand.
The app can be found in Play Store with the name Quick Cursor: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.quickcursor

It is an alternative to the already known Reachability Cursor app which, unfortunately, it is not maintained anymore (from 2018) and does not work on new Android versions.

I need help to collect any feedback on this early version. I'm interested in opinions about the idea, feedback on how it works on other devices, bugs, interesting features that might be helpful, etc. Anything you have to say about it!

Thanks HN!
